turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Morning, Mr.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Delacroix.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Can you give me your full name and date of birth for the chart? Raymond Delacroix, April 12, 1958.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thank you.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: How was the fishing trip you were planning? Oh, we caught a few redfish. My grandson outfished me, I won't lie.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Ha, that's how it goes. So, last time we started trazodone, 50 milligrams at bedtime, for sleep. How did that go? Well, I gotta be honest, I stopped it, after about 10 days.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: that's okay tell me what happened I'd sleep sure but in the morning I felt like I was walking through mud and one night I got up to use the bathroom and got real dizzy had to grab the dresser I'm glad you stopped it then and I'm glad you didn't fall did you hit anything no no fall just scared me so what's sleep like now without it back to the same I go to bed around 930 lie there an hour maybe two then I wake up about three and I'm up for good most nights. Are you taking anything to help?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: The Benadryl, the 25 milligrams, most nights, and melatonin, five milligrams. Okay, do you nap during the day?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: After lunch, an hour or so in the recliner. Since I retired from Crescent City Transit, there's not much else to do.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: And coffee, when's your last cup? I have two, one in the morning and one around three in the afternoon.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Do you watch TV every night that's how I fall asleep when I do does Bernadette ever say you snore loud or stop breathing at night no she says I sleep quiet she's the one who can't sleep she takes Ambien and swears by it any creepy crawly feeling in your legs at night and urge to move them no and how's your mood are you feeling down or worried a lot no moods fine I'm just tired okay your blood Blood pressure sitting is 134 over 80,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: and standing it's 130 over 78, so no real drop.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Pulse is 68. You're alert, a little tired looking, and your thinking is sharp. Your sleep questionnaire score is 18,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: which is moderate insomnia. Sounds about right.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: So here's what I think. This is chronic insomnia, and a lot of it comes down to sleep habits that keep it going,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: the nap,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: the late coffee, the TV in bed. bed. We won't restart the trasadone since it made you dizzy. I also want you to stop the Benadryl. At your age, it can cause confusion, dizziness, and falls.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Huh, I thought it was harmless since it's over the counter.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: A lot of people do. You can keep melatonin, but drop it to three milligrams an hour before bed.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Now the main plan. Get up at six,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: thirty every day, even weekends. Only go to bed when you're sleepy. No TV in bed.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: If you're awake more than about 20 minutes, get up,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: sit in the living room with a book, then go back when you're drowsy.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, what about the nap?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Skip it if you can, or 20 minutes at most before two o 'clock.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Last coffee by noon, and take a morning walk outside for the daylight.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I can walk the levee with my neighbor.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Perfect.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm also referring you to our CBT for insomnia program. It's a six session class, and it works better than pills long -term. Keep a sleep diary for the next two weeks. I'll put the form in your portal.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Is your email still ray .delacqua at bayoumail .com? That's it. Great.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let's follow up in six weeks. If you get confused or have a fall, call us sooner.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Will do. Thank you, ma 'am.
